items.title: Finite semisimple module category over a fusion category
items.statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a fusion category over $k$. A **finite semisimple right $\mathcal C$-module category** is a finite semisimple $k$-linear category $\mathcal M$ in the sense of [[def-semisimple-object-and-semisimple-abelian-category]], a bilinear action functor $\odot:\mathcal M\times\mathcal C\to\mathcal M$, and natural isomorphisms
$$\alpha_{m,X,Y}:(m\odot X)\odot Y\longrightarrow m\odot(X\otimes Y),\qquad \rho_m:m\odot\mathbf1\longrightarrow m,$$
which satisfy the module pentagon and triangle equations obtained from the associator and unitors of $\mathcal C$. The left-action convention is defined by reversing the order of the action factors.

A **module functor** $F:\mathcal M\to\mathcal N$ is a linear functor with natural action comparisons $F(m\odot X)\cong F(m)\odot X$ satisfying the module associativity and unit equations. A **module-natural transformation** is a natural transformation commuting with those comparisons. These objects, functors, and transformations form a 2-category denoted $\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal C)$ once its composition and monoidal product are specified.

This definition alone does not assert that there are finitely many equivalence classes of simple module categories, nor that $\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal C)$ is a fusion 2-category.

sources.title: Douglas and Reutter, Fusion 2-Categories and a State-Sum Invariant for 4-Manifolds, §1.4

items.title: G-graded finite semisimple 2-vector space
items.statement:
Fix an algebraically closed field $k$ of characteristic zero and a finite group $G$ ([[def-group]]). A finite semisimple category is understood in the sense of [[def-semisimple-object-and-semisimple-abelian-category]], with simple objects as in [[def-simple-object]]. A **finite semisimple $G$-graded $k$-linear category** is a finite semisimple $k$-linear category $\mathcal A$ together with a direct-sum decomposition
$$\mathcal A=\bigoplus_{g\in G}\mathcal A_g.$$
An object in $\mathcal A_g$ is homogeneous of degree $g$. A grading-preserving linear functor sends each $\mathcal A_g$ into the corresponding degree-$g$ summand, and its 2-morphisms are natural transformations. Such categories, functors, and natural transformations form the underlying 2-category denoted $2\mathrm{Vect}_G$.

For finite semisimple categories $\mathcal A,\mathcal B$ with simple-label sets $S,T$, their finite semisimple tensor product $\mathcal A\boxtimes\mathcal B$ has simple labels $S\times T$ and
$$\operatorname{Hom}(s\boxtimes t,s'\boxtimes t')=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A}(s,s')\otimes_k\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal B}(t,t'),$$
extended to direct sums. For a concrete skeleton, choose finite sets $S_g$ of simple labels and replace $\mathcal A_g$ by the category of finite-dimensional $k$-vector-space families indexed by $S_g$. A linear functor is represented by a finite matrix of finite-dimensional vector spaces within each grade. This skeleton fixes the meaning of “finite” and the homogeneous components; it does not assert any physical realization.

items.title: Separable algebra objects and bimodules in a fusion category
items.statement:
In a monoidal category $\mathcal C$, an **algebra object** is an object $A$ with multiplication $m_A:A\otimes A\to A$ and unit $\eta_A:\mathbf1\to A$ satisfying associativity and unit equations with the associator and unitors of $\mathcal C$. It is **separable** if there is an $A$-bimodule morphism $\sigma_A:A\to A\otimes A$ with $m_A\sigma_A=1_A$. The composite $e_A=\sigma_A\eta_A:\mathbf1\to A\otimes A$ is its **separability element**. It satisfies $m_Ae_A=\eta_A$ and the centrality equation
$$ (m_A\otimes1_A)\circ(1_A\otimes e_A)=(1_A\otimes m_A)\circ(e_A\otimes1_A):A\longrightarrow A\otimes A,$$
with associators inserted. In element notation these are $\sum_i x_i y_i=1_A$ and $\sum_i a x_i\otimes y_i=\sum_i x_i\otimes y_i a$.

A **left $A$-module** is an object $M\in\mathcal C$ with an associative unital action $l_M:A\otimes M\to M$; a **right $A$-module** has an associative unital action $r_M:M\otimes A\to M$. Write $\operatorname{Mod}^{l}_{\mathcal C}(A)$ and $\operatorname{Mod}^{r}_{\mathcal C}(A)$ for their categories and module morphisms. The category of left $A$-modules is a right $\mathcal C$-module category by $M\odot X:=M\otimes X$, with left $A$-action obtained by associating $A\otimes(M\otimes X)$ to $(A\otimes M)\otimes X$ and applying $l_M\otimes1_X$, and the inherited associator and unitor. An **$A$-$B$ bimodule** is an object $X\in\mathcal C$ with commuting left and right actions $A\otimes X\to X$ and $X\otimes B\to X$, each associative and unital. A bimodule morphism preserves both actions.

The **regular $A$-$A$ bimodule** is the object $A$ with both actions given by $m_A$.

Given an $A$-$B$ bimodule $X$ and a $B$-$D$ bimodule $Y$, a morphism $q:X\otimes Y\to Z$ is **balanced over $B$** if
$$q\circ(r_X\otimes1_Y)=q\circ(1_X\otimes l_Y):X\otimes B\otimes Y\longrightarrow Z.$$
A relative tensor product $X\otimes_B Y$, when it exists, is an object with a balanced map $q_B:X\otimes Y\to X\otimes_B Y$ universal among balanced maps. Existence is not part of this definition.

sources.title: Douglas and Reutter, Fusion 2-Categories and a State-Sum Invariant for 4-Manifolds, §§1.3 and 2.1.3

items.title: Weak linear 2-category
items.statement:
Fix a field $k$. A **weak linear 2-category** $\mathcal B$ consists of a class of objects and, for each ordered pair $(A,B)$, a $k$-linear category $\mathcal B(A,B)$. Its objects are called **1-morphisms** and its morphisms are called **2-morphisms**. Each triple $A,B,C$ has a $k$-bilinear composition functor
$$\mathcal B(B,C)\times\mathcal B(A,B)\longrightarrow\mathcal B(A,C),\qquad (g,f)\longmapsto g\circ f,$$
and each $A$ has an identity 1-morphism $1_A\in\mathcal B(A,A)$. A $k$-linear category here means that every hom set is a $k$-vector space and composition is bilinear.

For composable $f:A\to B$, $g:B\to C$, and $h:C\to D$, there is a natural invertible 2-morphism
$$a_{h,g,f}:(h\circ g)\circ f\Longrightarrow h\circ(g\circ f).$$
For each $f:A\to B$ there are natural invertible unit 2-morphisms
$$\ell_f:1_B\circ f\Longrightarrow f,\qquad r_f:f\circ1_A\Longrightarrow f.$$
The associators satisfy the pentagon equation on every fourfold composite; the two unitors and associator satisfy the triangle equation on every pair of composable 1-morphisms. These equations are equalities of 2-morphisms between the indicated parallel 1-morphisms. Vertical composition is composition in each hom category. Horizontal composition is the displayed functor, so functoriality gives the interchange equation between horizontal and vertical composition.

When the associators and unitors are identities, this is a strict 2-category in the sense of [[def-strict-two-category]]. No strictness is imposed in the weak definition.

sources.title: Douglas and Reutter, Fusion 2-Categories and a State-Sum Invariant for 4-Manifolds, §§1.1-1.2

items.title: The canonical algebra of a fusion category is Frobenius
items.statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a fusion category over an algebraically closed field. Write $\mathcal D=\mathcal C\boxtimes\mathcal C^{\mathrm{rev}}$, acting on $\mathcal C$ by $(X\boxtimes Y)\cdot V=X\otimes V\otimes Y$. Choose duals with $\operatorname{ev}_i:i\otimes i^*\to\mathbf1$ and $\operatorname{coev}_i:\mathbf1\to i^*\otimes i$. The canonical algebra $K=\underline{\operatorname{End}}_{\mathcal D}(\mathbf1)$ is $\bigoplus_i i\boxtimes i^*$, with multiplication induced by composition of evaluations and unit the inclusion of the unit summand. Projection $\lambda:K\to\mathbf1\boxtimes\mathbf1$ to that summand makes $\beta=\lambda\mu$ a nondegenerate pairing. Its inverse $c:\mathbf1\to K\otimes K$ defines a Frobenius comultiplication
$$\Delta=(\mu\otimes\mathrm{id})(\mathrm{id}\otimes c)=(\mathrm{id}\otimes\mu)(c\otimes\mathrm{id}).$$
This comultiplication is coassociative, is a $K$-bimodule morphism, and has counit $\lambda$, with $\lambda\eta=1$. No nonvanishing dimension or pivotal structure is assumed.

sources.title: Etingof, Gelaki, Nikshych, and Ostrik, Tensor Categories, Sections 7.20–7.21

items.title: Surjective orbit tangents give finitely many open orbits
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $k$ be algebraically closed of characteristic zero, let $G$ be a finite product of general linear groups, and let $X$ be a reduced affine variety of finite type with an algebraic $G$-action. If the differential of $f_x:G\to X$, $g\mapsto gx$, is surjective onto $T_xX$ at the identity for every $x\in X$, then every orbit is open and there are finitely many orbits. Empty products and the empty variety are allowed.

sources.title: Etingof, Gelaki, Nikshych, and Ostrik, Tensor Categories, Theorem 9.1.4

items.title: A separability element contracts the normalized categorical Hochschild complex
items.statement:
Let $A$ be an algebra object in a $k$-linear monoidal category and $B$ an $A$-bimodule. Suppose $e:\mathbf1\to A\otimes A$ satisfies
$$\mu e=\eta,\qquad (\mu\otimes\mathrm{id})(\mathrm{id}\otimes e)=(\mathrm{id}\otimes\mu)(e\otimes\mathrm{id}).$$
Set $C^n=\operatorname{Hom}(A^{\otimes n},B)$, with the Hochschild differential given by the alternating sum of the left action, adjacent multiplications, and the right action. Its normalized subcomplex consists of maps vanishing whenever any input is the unit $\eta$. For every $n\geq1$, define
$$h_n(f)=\lambda_B(\mathrm{id}_A\otimes f)(e\otimes\mathrm{id}_{A^{\otimes(n-1)}}),$$
where $\lambda_B$ denotes the left $A$-action. Then $h$ preserves the normalized subcomplex and $dh+hd=\mathrm{id}$ in every positive degree.

items.title: Relative Deligne product in the braided module 2-category
items.statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a braided fusion category and let $\mathcal M,\mathcal N$ be finite semisimple right $\mathcal C$-module categories. A **relative Deligne product** $\mathcal M\boxtimes_{\mathcal C}\mathcal N$ in $\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal C)$ means a finite semisimple right $\mathcal C$-module category $\mathcal P$ equipped with an exact bilinear functor $b:\mathcal M\times\mathcal N\to\mathcal P$ that is balanced over the middle $\mathcal C$-action and compatible with the outer right $\mathcal C$-action, and is universal among such functors: for every finite semisimple right $\mathcal C$-module category $\mathcal D$, composition with $b$ gives an equivalence between right $\mathcal C$-module functors $\mathcal P\to\mathcal D$ and exact bilinear middle-balanced right $\mathcal C$-module functors $\mathcal M\times\mathcal N\to\mathcal D$.

For the balancing convention, a right module category $\mathcal N$ is regarded as a left module category by $X\triangleright n:=n\odot X$. Its left module associator $(X\otimes Y)\triangleright n\to X\triangleright(Y\triangleright n)$ is the composite of $n\odot c_{Y,X}^{-1}$ with the inverse right-module associator. “Balanced” means that $b(m\odot X,n)\cong b(m,X\triangleright n)$ naturally in all variables, compatibly with the unit and associativity constraints. This definition fixes the universal property and the braiding convention; it does not assert that a product exists.

items.title: Weak monoidal 2-category
items.statement:
A **weak monoidal 2-category** is a weak 2-category $\mathcal B$ together with the following data.

1. A bilinear tensor pseudofunctor $\otimes:\mathcal B\times\mathcal B\to\mathcal B$. On 1- and 2-morphisms it has invertible comparison 2-morphisms for composition and identities, natural in each variable and satisfying the pseudofunctor composition and unit equations.
2. A unit object $I$.
3. Pseudonatural equivalences $a_{A,B,C}:(A\otimes B)\otimes C\to A\otimes(B\otimes C)$ and $\ell_A:I\otimes A\to A$, $r_A:A\otimes I\to A$. A pseudonatural transformation has a 1-morphism component at every object and an invertible naturality 2-morphism for every 1-morphism; the naturality squares for composites and identities commute. A modification between pseudonatural transformations has a 2-morphism component at every object, and its naturality square for each 1-morphism commutes. “Equivalence” means that an inverse pseudonatural transformation and invertible unit and counit modifications are supplied.
4. An invertible **pentagonator modification** $\Pi_{A,B,C,D}$ from the composite
$$a_{A,B,C\otimes D}\circ a_{A\otimes B,C,D}$$
to
$$ (1_A\otimes a_{B,C,D})\circ a_{A,B\otimes C,D}\circ(a_{A,B,C}\otimes1_D).$$
There are three invertible unit modifications, with sources and targets
$$\lambda_{A,B}: \ell_{A\otimes B}\circ a_{I,A,B}\Longrightarrow \ell_A\otimes1_B,$$
$$\rho_{A,B}: r_{A\otimes B}\Longrightarrow(1_A\otimes r_B)\circ a_{A,B,I},$$
$$\tau_{A,B}: (1_A\otimes\ell_B)\circ a_{A,I,B}\Longrightarrow r_A\otimes1_B.$$

All pseudofunctor comparison maps, transformations, and modifications are natural in their object, 1-morphism, and 2-morphism inputs. Their equations are part of the structure: the pentagonator obeys the five-object coherence equation (the two pastings between the endpoints of the 4-dimensional associahedron agree); the three unit modifications obey the triangle and double-unit equations; and inserting a unit in the five-object equation agrees with those unit equations. The tensor pseudofunctor comparisons satisfy their composition, unit, and naturality equations. These are equalities of parallel 2-morphisms; they are not consequences of object-level associativity.

The ordinary associator pentagon is represented schematically below. In a weak monoidal 2-category its two boundary composites are compared by $\Pi$, rather than required to be literally equal.

```tikzcd
& (A\otimes B)\otimes(C\otimes D) \arrow[rr,"a_{A,B,C\otimes D}"] & & A\otimes(B\otimes(C\otimes D)) \\
((A\otimes B)\otimes C)\otimes D \arrow[ur,"a_{A\otimes B,C,D}"] \arrow[dr,"a_{A,B,C}\otimes 1_D"'] & & & \\
& (A\otimes(B\otimes C))\otimes D \arrow[r,"a_{A,B\otimes C,D}"'] & A\otimes((B\otimes C)\otimes D) \arrow[ur,"1_A\otimes a_{B,C,D}"'] &
```

This definition uses the weak presentation directly. It invokes no global strictification theorem.

items.title: Opposite algebra induced by a braiding
items.statement:
Let $(\mathcal C,\otimes,\mathbf1,c)$ be a braided monoidal category and let $(A,m,\eta)$ be an algebra object ([[def-separable-algebra-and-bimodule-in-fusion-category]]). Define the monoidal opposite $\mathcal C^{\mathrm{mp}}$ to have the same objects and morphisms, tensor product $X\otimes_{\mathrm{mp}}Y:=Y\otimes X$, associator $\alpha^{\mathrm{mp}}_{X,Y,Z}:=\alpha^{-1}_{Z,Y,X}$, and unitors $\lambda^{\mathrm{mp}}_X:=\rho_X$, $\rho^{\mathrm{mp}}_X:=\lambda_X$. The braiding defines a strong monoidal equivalence $J:\mathcal C^{\mathrm{mp}}\to\mathcal C$ that is the identity on the underlying category and has tensorator $c_{Y,X}^{-1}:X\otimes Y\to Y\otimes X$.

Regard $A$ as an algebra in $\mathcal C^{\mathrm{mp}}$ with the same unit and multiplication $m:A\otimes_{\mathrm{mp}}A=A\otimes A\to A$. Its transport along $J$ is the **opposite algebra** $A^{\mathrm{op}}$ in $\mathcal C$; its multiplication is
$$m_{A^{\mathrm{op}}}=m\circ c_{A,A}^{-1}:A\otimes A\to A,$$
and its unit is $\eta$. This convention fixes the braiding direction. The hexagon identities are the tensorator coherence of $J$, and its unit coherence follows from the braiding unit equations.

sources.title: Douglas and Reutter, Fusion 2-Categories and a State-Sum Invariant for 4-Manifolds, §2.1.1

items.title: Canonical algebra modules and coherent tensor sliding
items.statement:
Use the canonical algebra $K$ in $\mathcal D=\mathcal C\boxtimes\mathcal C^{\mathrm{rev}}$ from [[lem-canonical-fusion-category-algebra-is-frobenius]]. Without a separability or characteristic-zero assumption, the functor $J:\mathcal C\to\operatorname{Mod}_{\mathcal D}(K)$ given by $J(V)=(V\boxtimes\mathbf1)\otimes K$ is an equivalence. There are natural right $K$-module isomorphisms
$$\rho_V:(V\boxtimes\mathbf1)K\longrightarrow(\mathbf1\boxtimes V)K.$$
They obey $\rho_{\mathbf1}=\mathrm{id}$ and the sliding equation: $\rho_{V\otimes W}$ is the composite of $\mathrm{id}_{V\boxtimes\mathbf1}\otimes\rho_W$, the interchange of the two separate Deligne factors, and $\mathrm{id}_{\mathbf1\boxtimes W}\otimes\rho_V$. In particular any right $K$-linear map $J(V)\to J(W)$ uniquely equals $f\otimes\mathrm{id}_K$ for $f:V\to W$.

sources.title: Etingof, Gelaki, Nikshych, and Ostrik, Tensor Categories, Proposition 7.18.5 and equation (7.57)

items.title: Right module internal ends and Eilenberg–Watts equivalence
items.statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a fusion category over an algebraically closed field $k$ and $\mathcal M$ a finite semisimple right $\mathcal C$-module category. There is an algebra $A$ and a right module equivalence $\mathcal M\simeq\operatorname{Mod}^{l}_{\mathcal C}(A)$. This assertion does not yet assert separability. Fix the convention
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(X,[m,n])=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal M}(m\odot X,n).$$
One can take $A=[m,m]$ whenever $m$ is a module generator, meaning every object of $\mathcal M$ is a quotient of $m\odot X$ for some $X\in\mathcal C$. In particular the direct sum of the simple representatives is such a generator. The multiplication is specified below. For any such algebras $A,B$, a right exact right module functor from left $A$-modules to left $B$-modules is uniquely, up to canonical isomorphism, $P\mapsto Q\otimes_A P$ for a $B$-$A$ bimodule $Q$. The equivalence identifies module-natural transformations with bimodule maps. No braiding is assumed.

For a finite semisimple left $\mathcal C$-module category and a generator $m$ with every $n$ a quotient of $X\odot m$, the left-action version is $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(X,[m,n])=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal M}(X\odot m,n)$ and $n\mapsto[m,n]$ is an equivalence to right modules over $A=[m,m]$, with $[m,X\odot n]\cong X\otimes[m,n]$. This version likewise does not require or assert separability.

sources.title: Etingof, Gelaki, Nikshych, and Ostrik, Tensor Categories, §§7.9–7.11

items.title: A uniform rank and action-multiplicity bound for module categories
items.statement:
For a fixed fusion category $\mathcal C$ over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, there is a finite integer $R(\mathcal C)$ such that every indecomposable finite semisimple right $\mathcal C$-module category has at most $R(\mathcal C)$ isomorphism classes of simple objects. More explicitly, write $I$ for its simple labels, $0$ for the unit, and $N_{ij}^k$ for its fusion coefficients. There are positive real numbers $d_i=d_{i^*}$, determined by these coefficients, with $d_0=1$ and $d_id_j=\sum_kN_{ij}^kd_k$. Put $D=\sum_i d_i^2$. One may take $R(\mathcal C)=\lfloor D\rfloor$. For every finite semisimple right module category, indecomposable or otherwise, the multiplicity $n_{ai}^b=[m_a\odot X_i:m_b]$ satisfies $n_{ai}^b\le D/d_i$. Consequently there are finitely many possible action multiplicity arrays at any specified rank, and finitely many indecomposable arrays at all ranks.

The real numbers used here concern the fusion ring, and are not categorical traces. No pivotal structure or positivity of categorical dimensions is assumed.

sources.title: Etingof, Gelaki, Nikshych, and Ostrik, Tensor Categories, Corollary 9.1.6
Etingof, Nikshych, and Ostrik, On fusion categories, Section 8.1

items.title: Module functor adjoints and separable-monad splittings in Mod(C)
items.statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a fusion category over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, and let $\mathcal M,\mathcal N$ be finite semisimple right $\mathcal C$-module categories. Every module functor $F:\mathcal M\to\mathcal N$ has left and right adjoints whose adjunction units and counits are module-natural. Every separable monad in the 2-category of finite semisimple $\mathcal C$-module categories has a separable splitting in that 2-category.

Here a separable monad is $(T,\mu,\eta)$ with a module-natural section $\sigma:T\to T^2$ of $\mu$ satisfying $T\mu\circ\sigma T=\sigma\circ\mu=\mu T\circ T\sigma$. A separable splitting means an adjunction $L\dashv U$ inducing this monad whose counit admits a module-natural section.

sources.title: Douglas and Reutter, Fusion 2-Categories and a State-Sum Invariant for 4-Manifolds, Theorem 1.4.8 and Appendix A.3
Etingof, Gelaki, Nikshych, and Ostrik, Tensor Categories, §§7.11–7.12

items.title: A separability idempotent constructs the balanced relative tensor product
items.statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a fusion category over an algebraically closed field $k$, let $B$ be a separable algebra object, and let $X$ be an $A$-$B$ bimodule and $Y$ a $B$-$D$ bimodule. Put $e_B=\sigma_B\eta_B:\mathbf1\to B\otimes B$. The endomorphism
$$p_{X,Y}=(r_X\otimes l_Y)\circ(1_X\otimes e_B\otimes1_Y):X\otimes Y\to X\otimes Y$$
is idempotent. Its image, with the induced map $q_B:X\otimes Y\to\operatorname{im}(p_{X,Y})$, is the relative tensor product $X\otimes_B Y$: for every object $Z$, composition with $q_B$ gives a bijection from morphisms $\operatorname{im}(p_{X,Y})\to Z$ to maps $X\otimes Y\to Z$ balanced over $B$. The result is independent up to a unique canonical isomorphism of the chosen splitting of $p_{X,Y}$.

sources.title: Douglas and Reutter, Fusion 2-Categories and a State-Sum Invariant for 4-Manifolds, §§1.3 and 1.4
Décoppet and Yu, Fiber 2-Functors and Tambara-Yamagami Fusion 2-Categories, §2.3

items.title: Finite semisimplicity for separable algebra modules and bimodules
items.statement: Let $A,B$ be separable algebra objects in a fusion category $\mathcal C$. The categories of left $A$-modules, right $B$-modules and $A$-$B$ bimodules are finite semisimple. This assertion is valid in any characteristic in which the stated separability sections exist. In particular the left $A$-modules, with action $P\odot X=P\otimes X$, form a finite semisimple right $\mathcal C$-module category.

sources.title: Etingof, Gelaki, Nikshych, and Ostrik, Tensor Categories, Proposition 7.8.30 and §7.11

items.title: A braiding gives the tensor product algebra structure
items.statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a braided fusion category with braiding $c$, and let $A,B$ be algebra objects. The object $A\otimes B$ is an algebra with unit $\eta_A\otimes\eta_B$ and multiplication
$$m_{A\otimes B}=(m_A\otimes m_B)\circ(1_A\otimes c_{B,A}\otimes1_B).$$

sources.title: Douglas and Reutter, Fusion 2-Categories and a State-Sum Invariant for 4-Manifolds, Construction 2.1.19
Décoppet and Yu, Fiber 2-Functors and Tambara-Yamagami Fusion 2-Categories, §2.3

items.title: Four-cocycle twisted monoidal structure on 2Vect_G
items.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite group ([[def-group]]), with identity $e$. A normalized multiplicative 4-cochain is a function $\omega:G^4\to k^\times$ equal to $1$ whenever any argument is $e$. It is a **group 4-cocycle** when, for all $g,h,k,l,m\in G$,
$$\omega(h,k,l,m)\omega(g,hk,l,m)\omega(g,h,k,lm)=\omega(gh,k,l,m)\omega(g,h,kl,m)\omega(g,h,k,l).$$

On $2\mathrm{Vect}_G$, define the tensor product by convolution:
$$\left(\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal B\right)_u=\bigoplus_{gh=u}\mathcal A_g\boxtimes\mathcal B_h,$$
where $\boxtimes$ is the finite semisimple tensor product of linear categories. The unit is $\mathrm{Vect}_k$ concentrated in degree $e$. The associator and unitors are the canonical rebracketing and unit equivalences. On four homogeneous inputs of degrees $g,h,k,l$, prescribe the pentagonator to be multiplication by the scalar $\omega(g,h,k,l)$ on every simple summand; extend it by direct sums and naturality. Denote this proposed weak monoidal 2-category structure by $2\mathrm{Vect}^{\omega}_G$.

The scalar is central, so its naturality is componentwise. The displayed group equation is the exact coherence condition to be checked for five homogeneous inputs. This definition includes no braiding and no claim about classification of all fusion 2-categories.

sources.title: Douglas and Reutter, Fusion 2-Categories and a State-Sum Invariant for 4-Manifolds, Construction 2.1.16
Décoppet and Yu, Fiber 2-Functors and Tambara-Yamagami Fusion 2-Categories, §2.1
Décoppet, Extension Theory and Fermionic Strongly Fusion 2-Categories, Example 2.2

items.title: Fusion 2-category
items.statement:
A **fusion 2-category** is a finite semisimple linear 2-category with a weak monoidal structure, a simple monoidal unit, and left and right duals for every object. For a right dual $A^\#$ of $A$, the duality data include 1-morphisms
$$e_A:A\otimes A^\#\to I,\qquad i_A:I\to A^\#\otimes A,$$
and invertible cusp 2-morphisms from $(e_A\otimes A)\circ(A\otimes i_A)$ to $1_A$ and from $(A^\#\otimes e_A)\circ(i_A\otimes A^\#)$ to $1_{A^\#}$, with the associator and unitors inserted at the indicated sources and targets.

Here “simple unit” means that $1_I$ is a simple 1-morphism. A pivotal or spherical enhancement is extra structure: it requires its own duality coherence and trace axioms. Neither such enhancement nor a spherical trace is included in “fusion 2-category.”

sources.title: Douglas and Reutter, Fusion 2-Categories and a State-Sum Invariant for 4-Manifolds, Definitions 2.1.5-2.1.6
Décoppet and Yu, Fiber 2-Functors and Tambara-Yamagami Fusion 2-Categories, §2.1

items.title: The braided tensor product of separable algebras is separable
items.statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a braided fusion category and let $A,B$ be separable algebra objects, with bimodule sections $\sigma_A,\sigma_B$. Give $A\otimes B$ the braided tensor-product algebra structure from [[thm-braided-category-tensor-product-algebra-structure]]. A separability section is
$$\sigma_{A\otimes B}=(1_A\otimes c_{B,A}^{-1}\otimes1_B)\circ(\sigma_A\otimes\sigma_B):A\otimes B\longrightarrow(A\otimes B)\otimes(A\otimes B).$$
This is an $A\otimes B$-bimodule map and its composite with multiplication is the identity.

items.title: Nonzero global dimension and the canonical Frobenius scalar
items.statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a fusion category over an algebraically closed field $k$ of characteristic zero. Use left duals $i^*$ with $\operatorname{ev}_i:i\otimes i^*\to\mathbf1$ and $\operatorname{coev}_i:\mathbf1\to i^*\otimes i$. For each simple $i$, choose an isomorphism $a_i:i\to i^{**}$ and put
$$d_i=\operatorname{ev}_{i^*}(\mathrm{id}_{i^*}\otimes a_i)\operatorname{coev}_i,\qquad e_i=\operatorname{ev}_i(a_i^{-1}\otimes\mathrm{id}_{i^*})\operatorname{coev}_{i^*},\qquad |i|^2=d_ie_i.$$
The scalar $|i|^2$ is independent of $a_i$. The global dimension $\operatorname{Dim}(\mathcal C)=\sum_i|i|^2$ is nonzero. Over $\mathbb C$, every $|i|^2$ is a strictly positive real number. For the canonical Frobenius algebra $(K,\mu,\eta,\Delta,\lambda)$ of [[lem-canonical-fusion-category-algebra-is-frobenius]],
$$\lambda\mu\Delta\eta=\operatorname{Dim}(\mathcal C)\ne0.$$
No pivotal or unitary structure on $\mathcal C$ is assumed.

sources.title: Etingof, Gelaki, Nikshych, and Ostrik, Tensor Categories, Sections 7.18–7.21

items.title: Relative tensor product gives associative composition of separable bimodules
items.statement: For separable algebra objects in a finite semisimple monoidal category, take objects to be separable algebras, 1-morphisms $A\to B$ to be $A$-$B$ bimodules, and 2-morphisms to be bimodule maps. Composition is $X\circ Y=X\otimes_B Y$ with order fixed so $X:A\to B$ and $Y:B\to D$ compose as $X\otimes_B Y:A\to D$. This composition has canonical associators and unitors satisfying the bicategory pentagon and interchange equations; its units are the regular bimodules $_AA_A$.

items.title: The canonical algebra of a characteristic-zero fusion category is separable
items.statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a fusion category over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero. For the canonical Frobenius algebra $(K,\mu,\eta,\Delta,\lambda)$ constructed in [[lem-canonical-fusion-category-algebra-is-frobenius]], set $t=\lambda\mu\Delta\eta$. Then $t\ne0$ and $s=t^{-1}\Delta$ is a $K$-bimodule section of multiplication. In particular $K$ is separable, and $e=s\eta$ satisfies
$$\mu e=\eta,\qquad(\mu\otimes\mathrm{id})(\mathrm{id}\otimes e)=(\mathrm{id}\otimes\mu)(e\otimes\mathrm{id}).$$

sources.title: Etingof, Gelaki, Nikshych, and Ostrik, Tensor Categories, Sections 7.20–7.21

items.title: Object duals in the separable-algebra model of Mod(C)
items.statement: For a separable algebra object $A$ in a braided fusion category $\mathcal C$, the object represented by $A$ in the separable-algebra/bimodule monoidal $2$-category has a left dual represented by the opposite algebra $A^{\mathrm{op}}$ of [[def-opposite-algebra-in-braided-fusion-category]]. There are evaluation $A^{\mathrm{op}}\otimes A\to\mathbf1$ and coevaluation $\mathbf1\to A\otimes A^{\mathrm{op}}$ bimodules, with invertible cusp $2$-morphisms identifying both snake composites with the respective regular bimodules. It also has a right dual represented by the positive opposite algebra $A^{\mathrm{op},+}$ with multiplication $m_Ac_{A,A}$; left and right opposites are not identified.

items.title: A normalized group 4-cocycle gives a fusion 2-category 2Vect_G^omega
items.statement: Let $G$ be a finite group and let $\omega:G^4\to\mathbb C^\times$ be a normalized group 4-cocycle. The convolution structure and scalar pentagonator of [[def-four-cocycle-twisted-monoidal-structure-on-2vect-g]] make $2\mathrm{Vect}^{\omega}_G$ a fusion 2-category. Its simple-object equivalence classes are exactly $\delta_g$ for $g\in G$, where $\delta_g$ is $\mathrm{Vect}_{\mathbb C}$ concentrated in grade $g$. The monoidal unit $\delta_e$ is simple. Every 1-morphism has left and right adjoints, every separable monad splits, and every object has left and right duals.

items.title: A normalized 3-cochain gives the gauge equivalence of 2Vect_G^omega
items.statement:
Let $\omega,\omega'$ be normalized 4-cocycles on a finite group $G$, and let $\beta:G^3\to\mathbb C^\times$ be a normalized 3-cochain. Define
$$\delta\beta(g,h,k,l)=\beta(h,k,l)\beta(gh,k,l)^{-1}\beta(g,hk,l)\beta(g,h,kl)^{-1}\beta(g,h,k).$$
If $\omega'=\omega\,\delta\beta$, then the identity on the underlying graded 2-category, with identity tensor and unit constraints and triple-input coherence modification $\beta(g,h,k)$, is a monoidal 2-equivalence $2\mathrm{Vect}^{\omega}_G\simeq2\mathrm{Vect}^{\omega'}_G$. Here $H^4(G;\mathbb C^\times)$ means normalized multiplicative 4-cocycles modulo coboundaries of normalized 3-cochains, with trivial $G$-action on $\mathbb C^\times$. Within this identity-on-grading gauge family, an untwisting to $\omega'=1$ exists exactly when $[\omega]=0$ in this quotient.

items.title: Categorical separability contracts the module deformation complex
items.statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a fusion category over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero. For finite semisimple $\mathcal C$-module categories, the normalized deformation complexes of a fixed module action and of a fixed module functor, defined below, admit an explicit homotopy satisfying $dh+hd=\mathrm{id}$ in every positive degree. In particular their degree-two cohomology vanishes.

Use left actions initially, writing $M_X$ and $N_X$ for the action functors on $\mathcal M$ and $\mathcal N$. For a module functor $T:\mathcal M\to\mathcal N$, use its comparisons $\gamma_X:N_XT\to TM_X$. Set
$$C_T^n=\operatorname{Nat}\bigl((X_1,\ldots,X_n)\mapsto N_{X_1}\cdots N_{X_n}T,\ (X_1,\ldots,X_n)\mapsto TM_{X_1}\cdots M_{X_n}\bigr).$$
Here $C_T^0=\operatorname{Nat}(T,T)$. The zeroth coface is $(\gamma_{X_1}M_{X_2}\cdots M_{X_{n+1}})(N_{X_1}f_{X_2,\ldots,X_{n+1}})$; the last coface is $(f_{X_1,\ldots,X_n}M_{X_{n+1}})(N_{X_1}\cdots N_{X_n}\gamma_{X_{n+1}})$. The $j$th interior coface merges $X_j,X_{j+1}$ and transports $f$ by the specified module associators. Their alternating sum, with signs $(-1)^j$ for $0\leq j\leq n+1$, is $d$. Normalization means zero whenever any $X_j=\mathbf1$, using the given unit comparisons. For $T=\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal M}$ these are the module-action deformation cochains. For a fixed general $T$ they are the module-functor deformation cochains.

For the right-action convention of [[def-finite-semisimple-module-category-over-fusion-category]], apply this definition to $\mathcal C^{\mathrm{rev}}$ and reverse the variable list: $M_X(m)=m\odot X$, and the action comparison is $M_YM_X\to M_{X\otimes Y}$. In particular degree two is the space of natural endomorphisms of $(X,Y)\mapsto M_YM_X$, after transporting through the fixed action comparisons.

items.title: Module-functor categories are finite semisimple
items.statement: For finite semisimple right $\mathcal C$-module categories $\mathcal M,\mathcal N$ over a fusion category over an algebraically closed field $k$ of characteristic zero, the category $\operatorname{Fun}_{\mathcal C}(\mathcal M,\mathcal N)$ of module functors and module-natural transformations is finite semisimple. In addition, evaluation at the tensor unit identifies $\operatorname{Fun}_{\mathcal C}(\mathcal C,\mathcal C)$ with $\mathcal C$ and sends the identity module functor to $\mathbf1_{\mathcal C}$; hence the unit object of the monoidal $2$-category is simple. Here “finite semisimple” means a $k$-linear abelian category with finitely many simple isomorphism classes, finite dimensional Hom spaces, and every object a finite direct sum of simples.

sources.title: Etingof, Gelaki, Nikshych, and Ostrik, Tensor Categories, §§7.11–7.12 and §7.21

items.title: Bounded-rank module-structure varieties have finitely many open orbits
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Fix a fusion category $\mathcal C$ over an algebraically closed field $k$ of characteristic zero. For each fixed possible rank of a finite semisimple right $\mathcal C$-module category, its module structures are represented, after choosing action multiplicities, by a finite union of affine varieties of finite type. The change-of-basis group on each such variety has finitely many orbits, each open, if the degree-two normalized action-deformation cohomology vanishes at every point. This vanishing is supplied by [[lem-modc-module-deformation-complex-contracts]]. Orbits on a fixed labelled action skeleton are equivalence classes of its normalized module structures with that labelling; forgetting labels can only identify further classes. There are consequently finitely many module categories of any fixed rank and finitely many indecomposable finite semisimple module categories up to module equivalence.

The finite union over action multiplicity arrays is essential: rank alone does not specify an action functor. No algebra classification or categorical trace positivity is assumed.

items.title: Finite semisimple module categories are separable algebra modules
items.statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a fusion category over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, and let $\mathcal M$ be a finite semisimple right $\mathcal C$-module category. There is a separable algebra object $A$ in $\mathcal C$ and a right $\mathcal C$-module equivalence $\mathcal M\simeq\operatorname{Mod}^{l}_{\mathcal C}(A)$, the category of left $A$-modules fixed in [[def-separable-algebra-and-bimodule-in-fusion-category]]. The construction below fixes the right-action/internal-Hom convention, gives the internal-end multiplication and a separability section, and proves full faithfulness and essential surjectivity. With these conventions, right module functors from left $A$-modules to left $B$-modules correspond to $B$-$A$ bimodules $Q$, acting by $Q\otimes_A-$; module-natural transformations correspond to bimodule maps.

sources.title: Etingof, Gelaki, Nikshych, and Ostrik, Tensor Categories, §§7.8–7.12 and §7.21

items.title: The relative Deligne product is represented by the braided tensor algebra
items.statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a braided fusion category and let $\mathcal M\simeq\operatorname{Mod}^{l}_{\mathcal C}(A)$ and $\mathcal N\simeq\operatorname{Mod}^{l}_{\mathcal C}(B)$ be finite semisimple right module categories represented by separable algebras; the left-module notation is fixed in [[def-separable-algebra-and-bimodule-in-fusion-category]]. Their relative Deligne product as fixed in [[def-modc-relative-deligne-product]] exists, is finite semisimple, and is equivalent as a right $\mathcal C$-module category to $\operatorname{Mod}^{l}_{\mathcal C}(A\otimes B)$, where the algebra product uses the braiding $c_{B,A}$. This equivalence is independent, up to canonical equivalence, of the chosen algebra presentations and supplies the object tensor product in the separable-algebra model of $\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal C)$. The relative products assemble into a weak monoidal $2$-category: associators and unitors are the unique equivalences preserving the relevant universal balanced functors, the pentagon and triangle modifications obey their coherence equations, and the product is compatible with module functors and module-natural transformations.

items.title: The algebraic 2-category Mod(C) is a fusion 2-category
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\mathcal C$ be a braided fusion category over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero. The 2-category $\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal C)$ of finite semisimple right $\mathcal C$-module categories, module functors, and module-natural transformations, with monoidal product given by relative Deligne tensor product over $\mathcal C$ (using its braiding to convert one action), is a fusion 2-category. In particular it is finite semisimple, has a simple unit, has left and right object duals, every 1-morphism has adjoints, every separable monad splits, and it has finitely many equivalence classes of simple objects.

items.title: Matrix 2-vector spaces exhibit horizontal and vertical composition
items.statement: In the ungraded component of $2\mathrm{Vect}_G$, identify $\mathrm{Vect}_{\mathbb C}^2$ with pairs of vector spaces. A linear functor is a $2\times2$ matrix of finite-dimensional vector spaces, and composition is matrix multiplication using direct sums and tensor products.

items.title: Typed object, 1-morphism, and 2-morphism defect composition
items.statement: In a chosen 2+1-dimensional defect theory modeled by a fusion 2-category, label objects $A,B,C$ as surface defects, 1-morphisms $f:A\to B$ and $g:B\to C$ as line junctions, and 2-morphisms $\alpha:f\Rightarrow f'$ as point junctions. This is a type dictionary conditional on that chosen theory, not a theorem identifying every algebraic object with a physical defect.

items.title: Relative tensor products of bimodules over C times C
items.statement: Work in the braided fusion category $\mathrm{Vec}_{\mathbb C}$ of finite-dimensional complex vector spaces, with ordinary tensor product and flip braiding. Let $R=\mathbb C\times\mathbb C$ with orthogonal idempotents $e_1,e_2$. For $i,j\in\{1,2\}$ let $M_{ij}=\mathbb C$ with left action through the $i$th coordinate and right action through the $j$th coordinate.

items.title: A C4 coboundary changes the pentagonator and is gauged away
items.statement:
Write $C_4=\mathbb Z/4\mathbb Z$ additively, with elements $0,1,2,3$. Define the normalized 3-cochain
$$\beta(g,h,k)=\begin{cases}-1,&(g,h,k)=(1,1,1),\\1,&\text{otherwise}.\end{cases}$$
Let $\omega=\delta\beta$, with the multiplicative coboundary convention in [[thm-three-cochain-gauge-equivalence-2vect-g]].

items.title: The trivial group gives ordinary 2Vect
items.statement: Take $G=\{e\}$. A $G$-graded finite semisimple category is just a finite semisimple $\mathbb C$-linear category. There is only one normalized 4-cochain, hence only one normalized 4-cocycle, and its pentagonator is the identity.
